title: What the Cornell Allegations Reveal About How America Raises Sons
author: Anthony B. Bradley
summary: Anthony Bradley uses the allegations against the so-called Cornell 7 to argue that a culture that prizes achievement over character produces young men who are impressive on paper and morally empty. Following a fraternity leader's remark that fraternities do not make terrible people, he says the men arrived on campus with their moral values already in place, shaped by a success-driven middle-class America that has purged religious formation. He offers the Catholic Catechism's account of the cardinal and theological virtues as an example of a far better framework, while stressing that he is not claiming every man must be raised Catholic. His conclusion is that parents must stop treating a strong resume as proof of a good kid and prefer moral excellence, since formation of heroic young men happens outside school. The piece is a short moral argument rather than a news report.
points: Bradley argues that fraternities provide context rather than cause, so the real failure is the moral formation boys receive at home before college.
He contrasts success defined by performance with success defined by the cardinal virtues of prudence, justice, fortitude and temperance.
The practical claim is that parents should prefer a morally excellent son over a credentialed one with no moral formation.
He suggests that teaching consent alone misses the point, because the goal is raising men to be virtuous.
quotes: What happened at Cornell is to be expected when success is defined by performance instead of moral virtue.
The truth is that these men arrived on campus with moral values already in place, and their fraternity provided a context for them to be the men they were raised to be.
As a society, we have purged religious formation as a concomitant framework necessary for true male success.
This is not about teaching men about consent. It’s about raising men to be virtuous, and that’s what our culture doesn’t care about today.
The “Cornell 7” is what happens when a culture raises young men to gain the world but does nothing to cultivate their souls.
We need to stop believing the myth that what makes a “good kid” a “good kid” is his résumé rather than his moral excellence.
America needs heroic young men on college campuses, and that formation only happens outside of school.
